findings.rationale: An independently-justified, source-driven RTF requirement (gp-accepted-standard__erc-4626__erc4626-totalassets-must-include-fees) exists, was generated from the real EIP-4626 spec text (not from H-01's description), was determined applicable to LiquidRon specifically, and would be routed to a real Codex investigation with a bundle carrying the exact fee-inclusion obligation directly on-topic for H-01's mechanism. This is the zero-cost-answerable question per §21 ('Did an independently justified RTF requirement exist? Was it generated? Was it applicable? Did it actually fire? Would the Codex agent have received it?') -- all confirmed yes with real evidence. Whether a real (paid, currently ungated) investigation against this specific requirement would correctly diagnose H-01's exact mechanism (operatorFeeAmount being a third-party claim, not a vault-level dilution fee -- a distinction EIP-4626's own spec text does not itself draw) is NOT claimed here and remains an open empirical question outside this preflight's scope.
findings.contrast_with_prior_architecture: Before this GP-generator work existed, a prior session's forensic A-E classification (rtf/l12_evaluation/SUPERVISED_VALIDATION_RERUN_2026-08-08.md §8, using only the static 81-requirement EthTrust corpus) classified H-01's miss as primarily 'E' (requirement-coverage limitation): no EthTrust requirement was shaped to ask this specific ERC-4626 accounting question, despite 4 independently-routed investigations reading the exact relevant code. This GP-generator closes exactly that gap at the requirement-generation level -- an ERC-4626-specific requirement now exists and correctly routes. Whether it also closes the gap at the INVESTIGATION level (a real agent actually producing an H-01-shaped finding from this more specific requirement) has not yet been tested with a real Codex call.
